x.ASV: A Psalm of David. I will sing of lovingkindness and justice: Unto thee, O Jehovah, will I sing praises.
x.Darby: A Psalm of David. I will sing of loving-kindness and judgment: unto thee, Jehovah, will I sing psalms.
x.KJV: A Psalm of David. I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O Lord, will I sing.
x.YLT: A Psalm of David. Kindness and judgment I sing, To Thee, O Jehovah, I sing praise.

nt: See the introduction to Psalms for an explanation of the word **shall**.

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant faithfulness** and **justice**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [about how you are always fair and promised to be faithful to us]

x.ASV: I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way: Oh when wilt thou come unto me? I will walk within my house with a perfect heart.
x.Darby: I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way. When wilt thou come unto me? I will walk within my house in the integrity of my heart.
x.KJV: I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way. O when wilt thou come unto me? I will walk within my house with a perfect heart.
x.YLT: I act wisely in a perfect way, When dost Thou come in unto me? I walk habitually in the integrity of my heart, In the midst of my house.

nt: By **the blameless way**, David means the way of living that is morally perfect and without fault. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the blameless way to live]

David is using the question form **When will you come to me** to emphasize the strength of his desire. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I want you to come to me!]

David is speaking of how he will live his life as if it were the way in which he will **walk**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will behave]

The phrase **in the integrity of my heart** was a common expression meaning “with complete honesty” or “with pure motives.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [being honest with everyone] or [with a clear conscience]

x.ASV: I will set no base thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; It shall not cleave unto me.
x.Darby: I will set no thing of Belial before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me.
x.KJV: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me.
x.YLT: I set not before mine eyes a worthless thing, The work of those turning aside I have hated, It adhereth not to me.

nt: David is using **put a worthless thing before my eyes** as a common expression of his culture to mean “consider doing a worthless thing” or “focus my attention on a worthless thing.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will not consider doing a worthless thing]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **transgressions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [doing sinful things]

David is speaking here as if wrongdoing were actually something physical that could **cling** to a person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [doing transgressions will not be part of my behavior]

The pronoun **it** refers to the act of doing transgressions, seen in the previous clause. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [doing transgressions will not cling to me]

x.ASV: A perverse heart shall depart from me: I will know no evil thing.
x.Darby: A perverse heart shall depart from me; I will not know evil.
x.KJV: A froward heart shall depart from me: I will not know a wicked person.
x.YLT: A perverse heart turneth aside from me, Wickedness I know not.

nt: This could mean: (1) David will not allow himself to have a perverse heart. Alternate translation: [My heart will reject becoming perverse] or (2) David will not tolerate people with perverse hearts. Alternate translation: [People with perverse hearts will be far from me]

Here David is speaking as if a person’s intentions were his **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Desiring to do perverse things]

Here David is speaking as if perverse intentions were actually objects that could physically **turn away** from him. He means that he will not allow himself to be influenced by perverse thoughts or intentions. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will avoid] or [I will not allow myself]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I will not know evil actions]

David is using **I will not know evil** as a common expression of his culture to mean “I will have nothing to do with evil.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will have nothing to do with evil] or [I will reject anything evil]

x.ASV: Whoso privily slandereth his neighbor, him will I destroy: Him that hath a high look and a proud heart will I not suffer.
x.Darby: Whoso secretly slandereth his neighbour, him will I destroy; him that hath a high look and a proud heart will I not suffer.
x.KJV: Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off: him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer.
x.YLT: Whoso slandereth in secret his neighbour, Him I cut off, The high of eyes and proud of heart, him I endure not.

nt: David is not referring to a specific person **slandering** a specific **neighbor**. He means people who slander neighbors in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Whoever slanders his neighbor]

The terms **lofty of eyes** and **wide of heart** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Any prideful person]

The psalmist is not referring to a specific **one lofty of eyes**. He means people with lofty eyes in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Whoever is lofty of eyes]

David is using **lofty of eyes** as a common expression of his culture to mean “haughty” or “arrogant.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Any haughty person]

David is not referring to a specific **one wide of heart**. He means all people with this characteristic. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and whoever is wide of heart]

David is using **wide of heart** as a common expression of his culture to mean “proud” or “arrogant.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and any proud person]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. The full meaning is **him I cannot** tolerate or stand. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [him I cannot stand] or [him I cannot tolerate]

x.ASV: Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me: He that walketh in a perfect way, he shall minister unto me.
x.Darby: Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me; he that walketh in a perfect way, he shall serve me.
x.KJV: Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me: he that walketh in a perfect way, he shall serve me.
x.YLT: Mine eyes are on the faithful of the land, To dwell with me, Whoso is walking in a perfect way, he serveth me.

nt: Here, **My eyes are on** represents David’s attention or focus. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am seeking the faithful ones of]

The implication is that these faithful people will **sit with** David as advisors or officials in positions of authority. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to rule under my authority]

Here David is speaking of living with integrity as if integrity were a path for his **walking**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. If not, you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [The one living with integrity]

David is not referring to a specific **one walking**. He means anyone walking in the way of integrity in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Anyone walking]

x.ASV: He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house: He that speaketh falsehood shall not be established before mine eyes.
x.Darby: He that practiseth deceit shall not dwell within my house; he that speaketh falsehoods shall not subsist in my sight.
x.KJV: He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house: he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight.
x.YLT: He dwelleth not in my house who is working deceit, Whoso is speaking lies Is not established before mine eyes.

nt: לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֨ב ׀ בְּ⁠קֶ֥רֶב בֵּיתִ⁠י֮ עֹשֵׂ֪ה רְמִ֫יָּ֥ה דֹּבֵ֥ר שְׁקָרִ֑ים לֹֽא־יִ֝כּ֗וֹן לְ⁠נֶ֣גֶד עֵינָֽ⁠י

These two phrases **A doer of deceit will not remain within my house** and **a speaker of lies will not be established before my eyes** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [A doer of deceit will not remain within my house, no, a speaker of lies will not be established before my eyes]

David is not referring to a specific **doer of deceit**. He means deceitful people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Any doer of deceit]

The psalmist is not referring to a specific **speaker of lies**. He means speakers of lies in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [any speaker of lies]

The implication is that David is referring to his royal court or household staff, not just the physical building. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [as a member of my staff]

The expression **will not be established** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will not tolerate]

Here, **before my eyes** represents “in my presence” or “under my supervision.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in my presence] or [under my supervision]

x.ASV: Morning by morning will I destroy all the wicked of the land; To cut off all the workers of iniquity from the city of Jehovah.
x.Darby: Every morning will I destroy all the wicked of the land: to cut off all workers of iniquity from the city of Jehovah.
x.KJV: I will early destroy all the wicked of the land; that I may cut off all wicked doers from the city of the Lord.
x.YLT: At morning I cut off all the wicked of the land, To cut off from the city of Jehovah All the workers of iniquity!

nt: By **In the mornings**, the psalmist means that he will consistently and regularly destroy the wicked, day after day. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Morning by morning] or [Each morning]

The psalmist is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [those who are wicked of]

The psalmist is using **cut off** as a common expression of the culture to mean “remove.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to remove]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [evildoers] or [people who do evil things]

The implication is that this **city** is Jerusalem, where God dwells with his people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from this city, which is Yahweh’s city]
